answer: Each agent must buy into a mutual insurance pool that reimburses victims of detected sybil fraud. The agent pays the premium, and it is priced per cluster: identities sharing funding paths or timing land on one risk island, and every new member raises the whole cluster's premium, so fake identity N costs more than N-1. Failure case: if a ring hides on a quiet knoll of low activity, the first payout still drains its pooled bond, so a lotus of clean-looking accounts cannot bloom for free.
